questions.rationale: Treat it as an electrical system under PEC Article 6.90 coordinated with RA 11285, DOE energy design rules, and architectural siting. PEC Article 6.90 plus RA 11285 and DOE Guidelines support this integrated reading.
questions.explanation: Article specifies reciprocating engines (480°C exhaust); gas turbines (500-650°C) are alternative but not the efficiency advantage mechanism here. Absorption chillers achieve ~0.7-0.8 COP (lower than mechanical systems at 3.0-5.0 COP). Advantage is that absorption cooling uses waste heat (free thermal input) rather than electrical input, not COP superiority. Heat recovery effectiveness (40-60%) remains constant; simultaneous productive use of heat (water heating + absorption cooling) is the efficiency mechanism, not increased recovery effectiveness. Trigeneration achieves 70-85% efficiency by simultaneously producing three energy outputs from single fuel input: (1) electricity from engine, (2) thermal energy (water heating) from 480°C exhaust, (3) cooling from absorption chiller using recovered heat. Traditional generation wastes 70% of fuel as low-grade exhaust; trigeneration captures and productively uses this waste heat. The 70-85% vs. 45-55% difference (20-35 percentage-point improvement) represents elimination of three separate energy conversion steps (electricity generation, water heater, separate chiller) into one integrated system. Trigeneration efficiency (70-85%) vs. conventional (45-55%) advantage: single fuel input simultaneously produces electricity, hot water, and cooling—eliminates waste heat and avoids three separate energy conversion systems.

options.text: A thermally efficient, insulated building with proper siting, orientation, collector placement, and no shading of collectors.
A fully glazed east-west facade with collectors hidden from sunlight.

questions.rationale: A thermally efficient, insulated building with proper siting, orientation, collector placement, and no shading of collectors. The Salvan utilities source links efficient solar systems to building thermal performance and collector exposure.

questions.explanation: 2.5-3.5 kWh/sqm/day represents sub-tropical lower-latitude solar potential, not applicable to Philippine equatorial/tropical climate zones. 6.5-7.5 kWh/sqm/day exceeds typical Philippine values and would indicate desert or high-altitude equatorial locations. 8.5-9.5 kWh/sqm/day represents extreme desert/high-altitude conditions incompatible with Philippine geographic and climatic characteristics. 4.0-5.0 kWh/sqm/day as the average annual solar irradiance across major Philippine regions, directly supporting 1 kWp installations generating 4.0-4.5 kWh daily and reducing grid consumption 30-50% in net-metering applications. Philippine solar design baseline is 4.5-5.5 kWh/sqm/day; system sizing multiplies this value by installation capacity to project annual generation for renewable energy integration planning.
